blocks.text: Memo: stay on Shopify for storefront, React only for admin later

This is the working cut for HBR-MEM-2021-077 on December 7, 2021. Dana Whitlock asked for a written bound after the current path (Shopify theme v1 in production, React not in the storefront path) stopped being honest. I am Michael Gilfilian, Web Developer, writing for Dana Whitlock, Jenna Park, and Nia Brooks. Primary host shop.harbor.internal. If you are skimming, jump the decision callout, then the refuse on custom React storefront, then open questions. If you are implementing next week, jump the constraints, the numbers table, and the commands or contracts.

Stay on Shopify for the customer site. A React admin for shelf counts can wait. Reject a custom Next storefront (~$28.5k, Dana becomes the PCI owner). I am not restating a hallway yes. custom React storefront is out because Dana does not want to own card data. Shopify already does. A nephew demo is not a PCI plan. Cost of doing nothing is already in the numbers: look at cost=28.5, theme=6.8, lcp=2.11, conv=1.31, weeks=16, pci=1, skus=412, admin=0. Sibling tickets HBR-2560 and HBR-REQ-2020-008. I will not reopen custom React storefront in a side thread because a vendor sent a discount. Jenna Park is the acceptor unless the owners line says otherwise.
Decision for leadership

blocks.label: Decision
blocks.text: Stay on Shopify for the customer site. A React admin for shelf counts can wait. Reject a custom Next storefront (~$28.5k, Dana becomes the PCI owner).

Background on shop.harbor.internal. Shopify theme v1 in production, React not in the storefront path. That is the system Dana Whitlock lives with, not a slide. I timed or pulled the leftover on admin.harbor.internal the week before this file. Lag, stale minutes, or miss counts in this file are from that pull, not a round number I liked. Ticket HBR-MEM-2021-077 names the pull. If those numbers moved after December 7, 2021, update this file in review, do not 'correct' them in Slack.

blocks.text: Background. Why the current path is the wrong tool

Nia Brooks owns a leftover that is easy to skip: stg-shop.harbor.internal. I will ping once. After that the owner is late, not blocked. Unique to this file (16): refuse on custom React storefront, lock is theme stays, React not funded this winter. I will not hide a product change inside a 'quick align' on HBR-2560.
I asked if we should rebuild the site in React because a nephew said so. I need you to say no in writing.

What a skeptical user would try first on shop.harbor.internal: the path Dana Whitlock actually has, not a desktop demo. Metric I will argue is time-to-useful, not a vanity QPS. If we cannot show that path on admin.harbor.internal with the numbers already in this file, we do not have a cut. Michael Gilfilian will not accept a laptop screenshot as that proof.
Constraints and the lock

What I will not claim in HBR-MEM-2021-077

I will not claim custom React storefront is impossible for a competitor. I will claim we will not buy it. I will not claim zero incidents after this cut. I will claim the next one dies at the gate named in the lock. Host shop.harbor.internal.
First useful slice for HBR-2560

First useful is theme stays, React not funded this winter, not a prettier theme or a bigger box. Dana Whitlock sees that slice on shop.harbor.internal. If the slice needs a second product, that is a new ticket and Dana Whitlock is in the thread. I will not hide it inside HBR-MEM-2021-077.
